findings.text: the delivered-status set now subtracts failed from the terminal vocabulary, but no arm of tests/test_a_delivered_runs_claim_lapses.py writes a manifest with status failed, so reverting the set to TERMINAL_MANIFEST_STATUSES leaves every test green while a failed run's claim would lapse after a day, widening the rule past the plan's "complete or blocked".

the ValueError arm is what keeps the claim when a manifest cannot be parsed, but no case feeds _delivered_status an unparseable manifest, so narrowing the tuple to OSError alone would let a ManifestParseError escape into the admission pass with nothing failing.

_delivered_status duplicates the fresh-manifest read owned by reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:2542 stopped_with_terminal_manifest — the same _manifest_freshness plus parse plus error handling, differing only in the accepted statuses and in not judging liveness — so the shared reader belongs in the manifest reader module; the commit extends that owner's vocabulary but wraps rather than extends dispatch_claims' read.

item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when names tests/test_a_delivered_runs_claim_lapses.py; the manifest records the head arm at 65 passed and the base arm at 58 passed, both EXIT=0, in after_suite-1795382569502014752.log and baseline_suite-1795382489561898807.log.
item_verdicts.goal: the node goal is that a delivered run nobody lands gives up its claim after a day; reckon/crew/claims.py:364 lapsed_claim_reason still implements it at this head, and the gained commit changes only how the delivered status word is read.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it states complete, names all three commits, records the repair round's arms (base 58 passed, head 65 passed) and cites negative-control-review-store.log, where each new case reddens under its own mutant.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the reviewed node declared eight write paths; the gained commit touches only reckon/crew/claims.py and tests/test_a_delivered_runs_claim_lapses.py, both inside that declaration.

justifications.durability: the two new cases are genuine guards, but no case writes a failed manifest, so reckon/crew/claims.py:184's subtraction of the failed status is unprotected, and no case passes a malformed manifest, so reckon/crew/claims.py:450's ValueError arm is unprotected.
justifications.evidence: tests/test_a_delivered_runs_claim_lapses.py:314 and :333 both fail under a recorded mutant with EXIT=1 in negative-control-review-store.log, and the caller importing the changed module reads the same two pre-existing ids at both revisions in exposed-caller-at-base.log and exposed-caller-at-head.log.
justifications.fit: reckon/crew/claims.py:184 derives the delivered set from the manifest reader's own constant, and the new docstring at :426 describes the mechanism without a plan, sprint or ticket identifier, matching the surrounding module.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/claims.py:405 still gates the lapse on _delivered_status, and the recorded head arm (after_suite-1795382569502014752.log:8) reads 65 passed at the reviewed head, so the deliverable behaves as the plan's §7 states.
justifications.reuse: reckon/crew/claims.py:426 still composes its own freshness-and-parse manifest read, duplicating reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:2542 stopped_with_terminal_manifest, although the vocabulary at :184 now extends that owner instead of restating its literals.
justifications.scope_discipline: git show --stat d17063f8..2fcfd78 lists only reckon/crew/claims.py and tests/test_a_delivered_runs_claim_lapses.py, both inside the node's eight declared write paths.
